steps.tx: **Psoriatic arthritis** or PsA affects up to **30 percent** of individuals with cutaneous psoriasis. Cutaneous plaques precede peripheral or axial articular symptoms by an average of **7 to 10 years** in the majority of cases. Nail lesions including **nail pitting**, hyperkeratosis, and **onycholysis** elevate arthritis risk **3-fold**, reflecting close anatomic enthesopathy linking the extensor tendon to the nail bed.
steps.say: Psoriatic arthritis affects up to 30 percent of patients with cutaneous psoriasis. Nail pitting and onycholysis indicate a 3-fold higher risk of developing articular disease.

vis.alt: Clinical photograph of nail pitting and onycholysis in psoriasis
vis.caption: Nail changes including pitting and onycholysis link closely to DIP arthritis. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: The **CASPAR criteria** classify psoriatic arthritis in patients with inflammatory articular disease. Classification requires **3 or more points** from 5 categories: current psoriasis scoring **2 points**, or personal or family history scoring **1 point**; typical **psoriatic nail dystrophy** scoring **1 point**; negative **rheumatoid factor** scoring **1 point**; current or past **dactylitis** scoring **1 point**; and radiographic evidence of **juxta-articular new bone formation** scoring **1 point**.
steps.say: The CASPAR criteria classify psoriatic arthritis using a threshold of 3 or more points. Points evaluate active or historic psoriasis, nail dystrophy, dactylitis, and periosteal new bone.

rows: Current psoriasis (2 pts) or history (1 pt)
Negative rheumatoid factor by any method
Current swelling or documented past history
Juxta-articular new bone on hand/foot films

steps.tx: Moll and Wright identified 5 clinical patterns of psoriatic arthritis: **asymmetric oligoarthritis** affecting fewer than 5 joints; **symmetric polyarthritis** resembling rheumatoid arthritis; **distal interphalangeal predominant** disease; destructive **arthritis mutilans** with telescoping digits; and **axial spondyloarthritis** presenting with unilateral sacroiliitis and syndesmophytes.
steps.say: Moll and Wright recognized five clinical patterns of psoriatic arthritis. Manifestations range from asymmetric oligoarthritis and DIP disease to severe arthritis mutilans.

vis.alt: Dactylitis and asymmetrical peripheral joint synovitis
vis.caption: Clinical patterns include dactylitis, asymmetric peripheral arthritis, and axial involvement. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: **Dactylitis** or sausage digit represents diffuse, uniform, painful swelling of an entire finger or toe. Occurring in up to **40 percent** of psoriatic arthritis patients, it reflects concomitant digital flexor tenosynovitis, enthesitis, and soft tissue edema. Dactylitis serves as an indicator of aggressive erosive disease and counts toward CASPAR classification.
steps.say: Dactylitis produces uniform sausage digit swelling affecting an entire digit. It reflects tenosynovitis and enthesitis, indicating an aggressive erosive disease course.

steps.tx: Radiographic hallmarks of psoriatic arthritis reflect the unique coexistence of bone erosion and pathological bone formation. Classic findings include the **pencil-in-cup deformity** from DIP marginal erosion, periostitis with **whiskering**, fluffy periarticular new bone, and non-marginal asymmetrical paramarginal **syndesmophytes** in the spine.
steps.say: Radiographs show concurrent bone erosion and bone proliferation. Characteristic findings include pencil-in-cup deformities, periosteal whiskering, and non-marginal syndesmophytes.

steps.tx: In peripheral psoriatic arthritis, **methotrexate** at **15 to 25 mg weekly** represents the standard first-line conventional synthetic DMARD, showing efficacy for joint and skin inflammation. Alternative csDMARDs include **leflunomide** and **sulfasalazine**. Notably, csDMARDs show zero efficacy for axial disease or enthesitis, requiring progression to biologic therapy.
steps.say: Methotrexate is the primary first-line conventional DMARD for peripheral psoriatic arthritis. Conventional synthetic agents fail to treat axial disease or isolated enthesitis.

rows: csDMARDs show no efficacy in spine

steps.tx: Biologic and targeted synthetic therapies for psoriatic arthritis encompass multiple mechanisms. **TNF inhibitors** including **adalimumab** and **etanercept** control joint and skin disease. The **IL-17A inhibitor** **secukinumab** and dual **IL-17A/F inhibitor** **bimekizumab** demonstrate superior cutaneous clearance. Oral **JAK inhibitors** like **tofacitinib** provide targeted synthetic alternatives.
steps.say: Biologic therapies include TNF inhibitors and interleukin-17 blockers. Secukinumab and bimekizumab provide high cutaneous clearance alongside durable articular control.

nodes.label: Initiate TNF inhibitor or IL-17 blocker
Rapid joint protection and skin clearance

steps.tx: **Deucravacitinib** is an oral, first-in-class allosteric inhibitor of **tyrosine kinase 2** or TYK2. By binding selectively to the regulatory pseudokinase domain rather than the active catalytic ATP site, it blocks receptor signaling for **IL-23**, **IL-12**, and **type I interferons** without inhibiting JAK1, JAK2, or JAK3, avoiding classical JAK-associated cytopenias and lipid disturbances.
steps.say: Deucravacitinib selectively inhibits TYK2 by binding its regulatory pseudokinase domain. This allosteric mechanism suppresses interleukin-23 signaling without traditional JAK inhibitor toxicities.

rows: Suppresses Th17 pathway and plaque formation
Avoids cytopenias, thrombosis, and lipid shifts
